ShortDescription.Value: Apply custom surfaces to road pavement, sidewalks, bike lanes and bus lanes, with reusable presets and junction controls.

## AI development and maintenance disclaimer
This mod was made using AI. I am not a developer and have zero programming knowledge, so I may struggle to fix bugs, keep the mod working after game updates, or maintain it over time.
Source code, bug reports and maintenance enquiries can be found on the project's [GitHub](https://github.com/Andy123k1/RoadSurfaceFiller) page, which you can find through the [official Cities: Skylines Modding Discord](https://discord.gg/HTav7ARPs2).
If you are a developer willing to help maintain the mod or take over the project, please contact me through that Discord. I am happy to discuss handing over the GitHub repository so the project can continue to be supported.
# Road Surface Filler
Give your roads custom pavement, sidewalk, bike-lane and bus-lane finishes using the surfaces installed in your game.
## Features - Save named styling profiles for each city and copy whole profiles or individual rules between setups. - Create reusable surface presets for different roads and lanes. - See surface thumbnail previews beside finishes in the surface pickers. - Choose whether editing a preset updates roads already using it or keeps their existing finishes. - Choose a preset while drawing roads, or use the road tool's Replace mode to restyle existing segments. - Apply general rules to existing roads with Apply city rules. - Activate the junction cycler and click junctions directly to cycle connected road and bus-lane finishes while keeping bike-lane surfaces visible. Right-click to exit the tool. - Fill adjacent paved bus-lane shoulders, or remove that shoulder fill from selected roads. - Convert generated surfaces into independent editable areas, with a tool to resume automatic updates later. - Restore selected roads or all roads to vanilla surfaces. - Manage rules in a movable, resizable panel with collapsible rule cards.
## Getting started Open the RSF button beside the Info button. Create a preset under Segment rules, then select it in the road tool's Surface rule picker. To apply general rules across existing roads, create them under General rules and choose Apply city rules.
Under Tools, choose Cycle junction surface, then left-click a junction or roundabout in the city. Each click advances its finish, and the tool stays active until you right-click or choose Exit junction tool.
## City styling profiles
Your shared General rules and Segment rules from before this update become Default automatically. Each city saves its own named profiles and selected setup.
1. Open RSF, then Profiles. Enter a name and choose Create empty profile for a fresh setup, or select Default and choose Duplicate current profile to start with your previous settings. 2. Choose the active setup with the Styling profile dropdown above the tabs. Changes stay with that city's profiles. 3. Use Copy from profile to copy an entire setup or individual General/Segment rules. Select a source, choose what to copy and, for a single rule, choose its destination profile. Rule cards also offer Copy to profile. Load another city once to make its profiles available as copy sources. Copies are independent. 4. Save General rules, then use Apply city rules to update existing roads. Select Segment rules in the road tool's Surface rule picker when drawing roads or using Replace. Presets retain their update preference for roads already using them. 5. Save your city to retain its profiles and selected setup.
Switching profiles keeps the Segment rules already applied to roads. Presets in inactive profiles retain their road links and update preferences. Converted editable areas keep their saved shapes and finishes regardless of which profile is selected, including after a profile is renamed or deleted. Choosing a profile alone does not repaint existing roads or resume automatic painting on converted roads. Deleting a profile removes its rule library while keeping placed finishes and independent areas; at least one profile must remain. Resume automatic surfaces remains an explicit tool action and keeps the independent areas.
## Manual surface editing Under Tools, choose Make generated surfaces editable, then click a completed road segment. Its surfaces become independent and the editor opens automatically. Drag boundary points or add points along edges to reshape them; each area keeps its existing finish. Use Edit another segment to convert additional roads and all approaches of a junction or roundabout. Finish editing exits the editor. Right-click cancels a drag; right-click while idle exits. Automatic updates stop on converted roads, and manual areas survive rebuilds, rule changes and road changes, including road removal. Restore all roads keeps these independent areas. Resume automatic surfaces reactivates saved road rules while keeping manual areas, so remove unwanted overlaps yourself. Keep this mod and the relevant surface assets enabled for these areas to render.
## Surface packs This mod uses available surface assets; it does not include the custom surface packs shown in screenshots. Install the packs containing the finishes you want to use. Only surfaces that support rendering over roads appear in the surface pickers. Those packs may have their own dependencies.
## Saved cities Segment finishes, junction choices and named styling profiles are saved with each city. Each profile contains its own General rules and Segment rules. Default starts with your shared rules from before the update. Create an empty profile or duplicate Default for a new city's style. Use the Profiles tab to copy complete profiles or individual rules between setups and cities; copies can be edited independently. Switching profiles keeps existing roads unchanged until you apply city rules or use the road tool. Save your city to retain its profile library.
Surface appearance depends on the road geometry and the selected surface assets. When reporting a problem, include a screenshot, the road type and the surface pack used.

# Version 0.5.39
Combines the city-profile updates from versions 0.5.37 through 0.5.39.
## Default and city styling profiles
- Saves General rules, Segment rules and named styling profiles with each city. Adds a Styling profile selector and a Profiles tab to create, rename, duplicate and delete profiles. Each city remembers its selected profile. - Makes the user's shared library from before the update the starting **Default**, including all General rules, Segment rules and saved segment update preferences. Captures this setup once in settings, including when it is empty. - Starts cities without profiles with an independent Default. Create an empty profile or duplicate Default for a different city's style. Changes in one city do not alter another city's profiles or the original Default setup. - Loading a city that already has profiles uses its saved library without adding an imported profile. Renaming or deleting a city's Default does not recreate it. The original Default remains available for deliberate copying. - Copies complete profiles or individual General/Segment rules between profiles and cities. Rule cards offer **Copy to profile**. Copies receive independent rule identities; copying a rule appends it without replacing the destination's existing rules. - Keeps matching saved segment links, update preferences and differing saved road definitions. Presets in inactive profiles remain available to their linked roads, and missing surface names remain identified. - Switching profiles keeps applied road finishes. General rules still require **Apply city rules**; Segment rules still use the road tool and each preset's update preference.
## How to use city styling profiles
1. Open the **RSF** panel. Your shared General rules and Segment rules from before this update are available as **Default**. No manual import is needed. 2. Open **Profiles**. For a new city or a different look, enter a profile name and choose **Create empty profile**. To start with your old setup, select Default first, then choose **Duplicate current profile**. 3. Use the **Styling profile** dropdown above the tabs to choose the profile you want to work with. Each city remembers its selected profile and keeps its own changes. 4. To reuse a setup, open **Copy from profile**, choose a source, then select **Entire profile** or an individual General/Segment rule. Whole profiles become new independent copies; individual rules are added to the destination profile you choose. Rule cards also offer **Copy to profile**. Load another city once to make its profiles available as copy sources. 5. Save General-rule edits, then choose **Apply city rules** to update existing roads. For Segment rules, select a preset in the road tool's **Surface rule** picker when drawing roads or using Replace. Each preset keeps its own preference for updating roads already using it. 6. **Save your city** to retain its profiles and selected setup. You can rename or delete your city's Default without it being recreated on the next load; the original Default setup remains available to copy from.
## What stays when you switch profiles
- **Placed segment finishes persist.** Switching profiles does not remove or reset the Segment rules already applied to roads. Linked presets in inactive profiles remain available to their roads and retain their update preferences. - **Editable areas persist.** Surfaces already converted with Make generated surfaces editable keep their saved shapes and finishes regardless of the active styling profile. Switching, renaming or deleting a profile does not erase those independent areas or resume automatic painting on converted roads. - **General-rule finishes stay until you apply changes.** Choosing a different profile alone does not repaint existing roads. Use Apply city rules or the road tool when you want to change their appearance. - **Deleting a profile removes its rule library, not its placed finishes or editable areas.** At least one profile must remain. Resume automatic surfaces is still an explicit tool action and keeps independent areas, so remove unwanted overlaps yourself.
## Profile deletion fix
- Fixes deleting the active profile disabling every tab and leaving the dropdown with a missing profile ID. - Selects a remaining profile before removing the old entry and automatically recovers an invalid saved selection. At least one profile must remain. - Keeps applied road finishes, junction choices and independent editable areas when removing a profile.
## After updating
- Restart with the updated mod and reload your city. Save the city to retain its styling profiles and selected setup. - Your previous shared library is available as Default. Create an empty profile or duplicate Default for a different city's style. - Switching profiles alone keeps existing roads and editable areas. Use Apply city rules or the road tool when you want to apply a different setup.
